pr.title: feat(local): route approved merge trains through the daemon
pr.body:
### Motivation
- Address #593. The reviewed merge-train tool has no caller in the running daemon, so independently approved stale PRs remain idle with model lanes disabled.

### Description
- Add a daemon adapter that matches a requested batch's pinned heads against the existing approved-candidate scan, checks claim availability, and prepares a clean primary checkout while preserving telemetry-only local commits.
- Invoke the existing train synchronously, retaining its combined CI, claim, lease and post-push checks. Keep individual merges as the existing default path and record refused or incomplete batches for reconciliation.
- Provide a runtime deployment patch, activation instructions and protocol notes. Runtime activation and the first live batch remain downstream of publication and independent review.

### Testing
- Published head `00e2079fb16f665721bf6b0fb209f07d22e0906f`: all nine local CI statuses passed in 410 seconds. All eight gates ran, including build, blueprint rendering, synchronization and statement-origin.
- The CI workflow suite and normal commit hooks each passed 736 tests with 9 skipped. The author also passed 26 focused adapter/claim/synchronization tests, including seven adapter cases.
- The rooted axiom audit passed 1,659 declarations with zero failures and three existing statement-level warnings. No proof-level leanok declaration depends on sorryAx.
- The runtime patch passed a zero-fuzz dry-run and its offline preview passed shell syntax validation. All six source-file hashes and three active-runtime hashes were verified; no daemon installation, restart or live train has run.

---
Addresses #593

issue.body:
<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: daemon-reviewed-train-scheduling-20260918 -->
The reviewed merge-train tool is on main through #507, and its member-title
policy is on main through #592 (b6c09eb0). The running model-free daemon
still invokes only the individual-PR path in /tmp/merge-v2.sh. Its current
implementation, /tmp/merge-daemon-v9k-cpa.sh, has no pr_train caller. With
PAR=0, approved stale candidates remain in its scans without an integration
attempt. Approved #580 and #587 are the first intended batch.

Connect the existing reviewed train to the actual daemon with the smallest
reviewable scheduling change. Preserve the current individual-PR path and
all existing train gates; do not build another transport or review system.

Required behavior and evidence:

- The daemon owns batch admission and invocation of local/bin/pr_train.py.
  MAIN must not invoke its publishing CLI by hand. Use the existing service
  controls and one publication flow; do not start a parallel merger.
- Admit only independently approved exact heads with green CI and respect
  the shared claim list. The train's own current-head, dependency, combined
  CI, claim, lease and post-push checks remain authoritative.
- Prevent the same daemon from moving main through individual merges or
  telemetry commits while its train is integrating and validating. Keep
  the current telemetry batching discipline around the publication window.
- Keep PAR=0 and all model lanes disabled. A refused or conflicting batch
  must be recorded truthfully and must not be reported as merged.
- Provide focused offline evidence for batch routing and refusal handling,
  then follow the normal review/deployment process for any changed code.
  Reuse the merged train's validation rather than rerunning its design review.
- After deployment, run the first eligible batch through the daemon and
  verify GitHub's merged state, actual integrated member heads, first-parent
  subjects with Lean deltas, claims release and retained integration evidence.

The owner's accepted claims/leased atomic push/post-push verification contract
and residual window remain unchanged. No server-side predicate is required.
Issue #589 separately tracks interrupted-claim recovery and diagnostics;
that follow-up is not a prerequisite for this scheduling work. No live train
has run yet. This issue tracks the remaining operational use of the already
reviewed tool, rather than another train implementation.
